subject: History
name: Basic 2 History
description: The Basic 2 History curriculum focuses on the people of Ghana, their ethnic groups and characteristics, major historical locations, significant Ghanaian women, and the history of European trade in Ghana.

strands.title: My Country Ghana
strands.description: Exploring the people, historical locations, and significant individuals of Ghana.

subStrands.title: The People of Ghana
subStrands.description: Understanding the ethnic groups and their characteristics.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge of the ethnic groups in Ghana

indicators.description: Identify the ethnic groups in each region in Ghana

exemplars.description: Identify the administrative regions of Ghana.
Locate the ethnic groups in each region on a map of Ghana.
With the aid of a slide/video/TV/internet, identify the regions and ethnic groups in Ghana.
Match the ethnic groups with their region.
List the administrative regions in the order in which they created (starting with the oldest region).

contentStandards.description: Show understanding of the characteristics of some of the ethnic groups in Ghana

indicators.description: State the characteristics of the ethnic groups in Ghana

exemplars.description: Identify the characteristics (food, festivals, dressing, language, political institutions, social and economic activities, taboos, oaths etc.) of some of the ethnic groups in Ghana.
Show documentary/pictures/ internet of a festival of one of the ethnic groups.
Discuss what the documentary entails.

subStrands.title: Major Historical Locations
subStrands.description: Exploring the history of major locations in Ghana.

contentStandards.description: Exhibit knowledge of the history of the major historical locations in Ghana

indicators.description: Discuss the history of Ghana's major historical locations.

exemplars.description: Identify the major historical locations in Ghana (starting with the oldest location).
Show and discuss video/documentary/stories/slides about the history of these major historical locations in Ghana.
Retell the history of these major historical locations in Ghana.
Interact with knowledgeable persons/ opinion leaders/ chiefs/ resource persons to tell the history of any historical location in your community or district.
Visit any historical site in their community.
Retell the history of major sites in their community.

subStrands.title: Some Selected Individuals
subStrands.description: Highlighting the contributions of Ghanaian women to national development.

contentStandards.description: Exhibit understanding of Ghanaian women who have contributed significantly to Ghana's development

indicators.description: Identify Ghanaian women who have made significant contributions to national development

exemplars.description: Name some outstanding women in the history of Ghana.

Match these women with their achievements in Ghana e.g. Mrs Charity Zormelo-Fiawoo - first woman university graduate; Squadron Leader Melody Danquah - First female pilot; Elizabeth Ohene - First female editor of a newspaper (Daily Graphic); Justice Georgina Wood - First female Chief Justice; Justice Joyce Bamford-Addo - First female Speaker of Parliament etc.
Using anecdotes/videos learners retell the contributions of these leaders to national development.
Think pair-share-activity: Individual learners identify a woman who they admire most in the community. They choose partners and discuss the reasons for their choice.

strands.title: Europeans in Ghana
strands.description: Understanding the history of European contact and trade.

subStrands.title: International Trade Including Slave Trade
subStrands.description: Examining the nature of early trade between Ghanaians and Europeans.

contentStandards.description: Understand that trade was the major reason why the Europeans settled in Ghana

indicators.description: Describe how early trade was carried out between Ghanaians and Europeans

exemplars.description: Describe how early trade was carried out between Ghanaians and the Europeans.
Organise learning corners with real items or pictures of items brought by the Europeans such as Gin, Gun, Gun Powder, Textiles, Tobacco, Iron Bars, Elephant tusks, Ivory, Gold.
Role play the barter trade in those items.
Use internet to identify countries with the items they brought that remained part of everyday Ghanaian life. e.g. the Dutch and wax prints.
Name the towns that emerged on the coast as a result of European trade with Ghanaians.
